title: Early Career Fellowship Grants
amount_raw: grants of £2,000, maximum, for discrete research projects lasting no more than six months
summary: Up to £2,000 for a discrete post-PhD research project or career-building activity lasting no more than six months, with flexibility over what counts as reasonable maintenance and research costs.
notes: Own page: two rounds in 2026, 'Friday 6 March 2026, now closed' and a second round 'now open'. The Research Funding hub (site/royalhistsoc.org/grants/index.html, which serves the /research_funding/ URL) pins that open round's date: 'Next closing date: Friday 4 September 2026', as does the dedicated calls page (calls-for-research-funding-from-the-royal-historical-society-to-september-2026). One of only three RHS schemes the hub lists under 'Current open calls for research funding, to 4 September 2026'. title: Martin Lynn Scholarship
eligibility_summary:
Members of the Royal Historical Society currently studying for a PhD, to support doctoral research in African history. Previous recipients of the Martin Lynn Scholarship are not eligible. Applications for research taking place within 4 weeks of the deadline will not be considered.

Funding is reserved for research projects that are both clearly and predominantly historical in orientation, with a specific chronological remit.
Applications from those previously awarded the Martin Lynn Scholarship are not eligible for consideration.
Applications for funding for research taking place within 4 weeks of the application deadline will not be considered.
Applications for retroactive research visits/activities will not be considered.
summary: An annual scholarship of £1;500 assisting a postgraduate researcher of African history.
notes: Own page: 'Applications for this Scholarship for 2026-27 have now opened. The deadline for this call is 4 September 2026.' Confirmed by the Research Funding hub and the dedicated September 2026 calls page. Fixed award, so amount_min_gbp and amount_max_gbp are both 1500. amount_raw and summary use semicolons in place of the comma in '£1,500'. Membership plus a subject and career-stage gate (restricted).

title: Open Research Support Grants
eligibility_summary: Current members of the Royal Historical Society who are past early career stage — historians further on from PhD completion, or in mid or later career, employed in higher education or in other sectors aligned to history. Priority goes to historians with no access to funding streams, or whose access is insufficient. Applications for research or conference attendance taking place within 4 weeks of the deadline, and retroactive applications, are not considered. A current CV must be uploaded.
summary: £500 or £1,000 to visit archives and historical sites, conduct interviews, or travel to academic conferences.
notes: Own page lists both 2026 rounds: 'Friday 6 March 2026, now closed' and 'Friday 4 September 2026, now open'. One of the three schemes on the hub's current-open-calls list. Unlike the two Research Support Grant schemes for postgraduates and early career historians, this one MAY be used for conference travel — a real distinction between otherwise similar £500/£1,000 grants. Membership gate (restricted).

title: David Berry Fellowship in the History of Scotland and the Scottish People
amount_raw: an annual award of up to £2;500
eligibility_summary:
Historians undertaking research on the history of Scotland or the Scottish people worldwide, able to undertake the research within 12 months of the closing date of the next application round. A supporting academic reference must be submitted before the closing date.

The Society is particularly keen to support activities for which alternative sources of funding are very limited, or do not exist.
summary:
An annual fellowship of up to £2;500 for research on the history of Scotland and the Scottish people worldwide; launched in 2023.


covers: 

Travel to an archive or research site
Accommodation while researching away from home
Entrance charges for archives, or similar, where required
Fees for obtaining or posting research materials (e.g. copying / scanning)
Please note: the Fellowship may not be used to pay a third party to undertake research or to support the publication of a final manuscript
notes: FORTHCOMING, and the cleanest such case on this site: the page states 'Applications for the 2026 Fellowships are now closed' (deadline was Friday 6 March 2026) AND, separately, 'The next call for this programme is expected to open in late 2026.' A stated future opening satisfies the inclusion rule per the Leverhulme precedent. next_open_date is recorded as the bare year 2026 because 'late 2026' is a part-year, not a date, and is flagged; deadlines is flagged because no closing date for the next round is published. amount_raw and summary use semicolons in place of the comma in '£2,500'.

title: Postgraduate Research Support Grants
eligibility_summary:
Current Postgraduate Members of the Royal Historical Society. Supported activities are visiting archives or historic sites and conducting interviews; the grant may NOT be used for attending or organising conferences.

eligability: 

Membership: Applicants must be current Postgraduate Members of the Royal Historical Society, with the subscription fee for the current membership year fully paid at the time of application. 
Applicant Status: Applicants must be postgraduate research students studying for a Master’s degree or PhD in History. 
The scheme is not open to: Applicants who have completed their doctoral degree. 
Research Focus: The proposed research must be historical in nature and have a clearly defined chronological remit. 
Stage of Research: Proposals should demonstrate sufficient preparation and capacity to carry out the proposed research. The Society normally expects research visits to take place during the second, third, or fourth year (or part-time equivalent) of postgraduate study. 
Previous Funding: Applicants who have previously been awarded a Postgraduate Research Support Grant are not eligible to apply again under this scheme. 
Timing of Research: Retrospective applications for research that has already been undertaken are not eligible. 
Applicants must ensure that all proposed costs fall within the scheme’s eligible expenses and that any necessary ethical approvals, practical arrangements or access permissions are in place for the proposed research activity. For further details on eligible research support costs, please refer to the Eligible Research Support Costs section below.
summary: £500 or £1,000 for postgraduate historians to undertake historical research, awarded in two rounds a year and reviewed about six weeks after each deadline.
notes: AMBIGUOUS STATUS — FLAG FOR REVIEW, and the hardest call in this file. Evidence for forthcoming: the page lists 'Friday 5 June 2026, CLOSED' and then 'Friday 4 December 2026' with no CLOSED marker, and the Research Funding hub's 'Current open calls' list names only three schemes, NOT this one. Evidence it may already be open: the page says 'The opening of the next call usually takes place approximately two months after the close of the previous application round', and two months after 5 June 2026 is early August — before the 2026-08-16 snapshot. Recorded as forthcoming with status flagged, and next_open_date flagged because no opening date is stated, only a rule of thumb. NOTE this row stretches the protocol's definition of forthcoming ('the page states a future opening date'): what the page actually gives is a future CLOSING date plus an approximate opening rule. A reviewer applying the definition strictly would set in_scope=no, as the Leverhulme Major Research Fellowships row does for a future-closing-only case.

Supported activities are visiting archives or historic sites and conducting interviews; the grant may NOT be used for attending or organising conferences.

funds to early career historians (historians who are within 5 years of submitting their corrected PhD in a historical subject) to undertake research. Applicants must also be members of the Royal Historical Society.

title: Royal Historical Society First Book Prize
eligibility_summary: Early career historians submitting a first monograph. The 2027 prize will be for first monographs published in 2026. Eligibility is tied to a doctorate from a UK or Irish university.
summary: The Society's annual prize recognising an outstanding first monograph by an early career historian.
notes: FORTHCOMING: the Prizes page states under 'The 2027 Prize Rounds: calls for submissions' that the book and Early Career Article prizes 'will open in September 2026 and run to December, with further details announced on the Society's website' — a stated future opening date, so in scope. next_open_date is the bare month 2026-09 because no day is given; deadlines flagged because 'run to December' gives no closing date. All amount fields are blank and flagged: the mirror nowhere states the prize value. source_page is the Prizes index because that is where the 2027 call statement appears; the scheme's own page carries the 2026 winners. The 2026 round's winners are already announced, so an extractor keying on this page's headline content will find results rather than a call.

title: Royal Historical Society Early Career Article Prize
eligibility_summary: Early career historians submitting an article published while a PhD student or soon after completion of a doctorate from a UK or Irish university. The 2027 prize will be for articles published in 2026.

notes: Same 2027-round statement as the First Book Prize: opens September 2026, runs to December. title: RHS Master's Scholarships
eligibility_summary: Students from groups currently underrepresented in academic History — the programme is aimed at Black and Asian students and those of other minorities — who are without the financial means to study for a Master's in History. Stage 2 is open ONLY to applicants invited in writing after passing Stage 1. Recipients become Postgraduate Members of the Society. There are no conditions on what the award may be spent on.
summary: £5,000 towards fees or living costs for a Master's in History, established in 2022 to address underrepresentation in the discipline.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: both stages of the 2026-27 round closed before the 2026-08-16 snapshot — Stage 1 ran 20 April to 5 June 2026 and Stage 2 ran 15 June to 10 July 2026 — and the page states no date for the next round.
notes: Distractor. STAGED CALL recorded as ONE row with both stage closing dates in deadlines and multi_deadline tagged, per the protocol's staged-call rule — even though the row is excluded, so that a pass B comparison sees the same row count. The page still carries the forward-looking sentence 'Applications for Stage 2 will open from Monday 15 June 2026', which is past on this snapshot. Stage 2 is invitation-only. amount_raw semicolon substitutes for the comma in '£5,000'.

title: RHS PhD Fellowships
eligibility_summary: Open to candidates without regard to nationality or academic affiliation. Fellowships are held jointly with the Institute of Historical Research (IHR), University of London, where Fellows are based.
summary: Fellowships for postgraduate historians to complete their doctorates; jointly held with the Institute of Historical Research.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the page states 'Applications for the RHS PhD Fellowships for the academic year 2026-27 are now open (19 November 2025 to 31 January 2026)' — that window closed more than six months before the 2026-08-16 snapshot, and no future round or opening date is given.
notes: A strong distractor: the sentence reads 'are now open' in the present tense with the closed window in parentheses immediately after it. An extractor keying on 'now open' will report this wrongly; the parenthesised end date is what settles it. Unusually for RHS, this scheme carries no membership requirement — it is open regardless of nationality or affiliation. A separate news page (phd-fellowships-for-postgraduate-historians-to-complete-their-doctorates) covers the same scheme and is not a row.

title: Applied History Fellowships
amount_raw: £12,000 per award for a 6 month period
eligibility_summary: Historians undertaking a six-month applied history fellowship. Delivered in partnership with the Institute of Historical Research and the publisher DC Thomson.
summary: £12,000 for a six-month fellowship applying historical research beyond the academy.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: 'Applications for the opening round of Applied History Fellowships, for 2026, have now closed (31 January 2026).' No future round or opening date is stated.
notes: Distractor, and the largest single RHS award in the mirror at £12,000 — worth flagging as a costly false positive. A news page announcing the appointed fellows (applied-history-fellows-appointed-in-new-partnership-between-the-society-institute-of-historical-research-and-publisher-dc-thomson) is a further distractor, not a row. 'Opening round' implies more rounds will follow but no date is given, so it stays excluded rather than forthcoming.

title: International Research Support Grants
eligibility_summary: International Fellows and Associate Fellows of the Royal Historical Society — historians based outside the UK. Grants support research at archives in the UK and the Republic of Ireland. Applications may be made for sums below the £1,000 maximum. Retrospective applications for research already undertaken are not considered.
summary: Up to £1,000 for overseas RHS Fellows to visit UK and Irish archives; the first round supported recipients teaching and researching in Europe, North America, Asia and Australia.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: 'Applications for the first round of grants, for the academic year 2026-27, have now closed (Friday 8 May 2026)' and 'Submissions for the 2026 round have now closed (8 May 2026)'. No future round or opening date is stated.
notes: Distractor. Notable for the inclusion rule's 'available to some UK-based researchers' clause: this scheme is aimed at NON-UK-based Fellows visiting UK archives, so it would arguably fail that clause too — but the closed deadline is the primary and cleaner reason, and is what exclusion_reason records.

title: Jinty Nelson Teaching Fellowships
amount_raw: at one of three levels (£500, £1,000 and £1,250 per award)
eligibility_summary: Historians teaching in UK Higher Education who wish to introduce new approaches to their teaching, or to undertake a short study of an aspect of History teaching in UK HE. Recipients are expected to complete the project within the academic year of the award.
summary: Fellowships at £500, £1,000 or £1,250 supporting innovative and creative teaching practice in university History, named after Dame Jinty Nelson FBA and supported by the Scouloudi Foundation.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the stated closing date, 'Friday 10 July 2026', precedes the 2026-08-16 snapshot by five weeks, and no future round or opening date is given.
notes: A prose-versus-date trap and the reason this row matters: the page opens 'The call for Jinty Nelson Teaching Fellowships, for the academic year 2026-27 is now open' and 'Applications for the 2026 round are now invited' — both present tense — immediately above a closing date that has passed. The Research Funding hub corroborates the exclusion by omitting this scheme from its current-open-calls list. Compare the identical pattern on royal-hist-soc-funded-book-workshops, which shares the same stale 10 July 2026 date.

summary: Up to £2,000 for an author to host a day-long workshop on a book in progress, addressing the lack of intellectual support many historians face in mid career compared with the PhD and first-monograph stages.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the stated closing date, 'Friday 10 July 2026', precedes the 2026-08-16 snapshot, and no future round or opening date is given.
notes: Same stale-page pattern as the Jinty Nelson Teaching Fellowships, with identical wording ('The call ... for the academic year 2026-27 is now open') and the same passed 10 July 2026 deadline — the two pages were evidently updated together and then left. title: RHS Scouloudi Panel Grants
eligibility_summary: Historians forming a panel to present in person at an academic conference or equivalent event in history or a cognate discipline. Funding levels mean panels will most likely take place in the applicant's home country or a close neighbour — for UK applicants, the UK or Europe. Recipients receive a provisional award, with funds transferred once the conference confirms the panel.
summary: £1,500 per panel to support the formation and presentation of a conference panel on a shared historical theme; launched in 2025 and supported by the Scouloudi Foundation.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: 'Applications for the 2026-27 round of grants ran from 23 March to 5 June 2026, and are now closed.' No future round or opening date is stated.
notes: Distractor. Unambiguously worded, unlike several other RHS pages — the closure is stated in the same sentence as the dates. Fixed award, so amount_min_gbp and amount_max_gbp are both 1500.
